title: The Things I Let Him See
sub_niche: dark psychological thriller-romance, single first-person POV, surveillance cat-and-mouse, domestic gaslighting, slow-burn romance with explicit consent
hook_central: A surveillance operative hired to prove a separated wife unstable becomes obsessed with her ordinary routines, unaware that she identified him almost immediately and has begun designing what he sees.

female.name: Calder Reed
female.voice: Measured, deliberate, uses precise language; often pauses before responding; rarely raises her voice; can be devastatingly calm under pressure.
tics: Arranges objects in precise grid on desk before starting work
Checks red receipts twice before filing
female.boundary: Will not allow anyone to make decisions for her; refuses to be rescued; will cut contact if someone overrides her choice.
female.internal_voice: I am not unstable. I am not confused. I am watching him watch me.

male.name: Calder
male.voice: Terse, observational, often internal; speaks in short declarative sentences; rarely volunteers personal information; uses clinical terms for emotions.
tics: Taps the camera lens before each session
Keeps left hand in pocket when uncertain
Repeats the subject's last words under his breath
male.boundary: Refuses to violate his own archive integrity; will not destroy evidence even for personal gain; cannot tolerate being deceived.
male.wound: His previous surveillance contract ended in a false report that ruined an innocent subject; he never verified before submitting.

supporting_cast.name: Grant
supporting_cast.secret: Orchestrated the surveillance contract and edited the dashboard to conceal his own gaslighting.

supporting_cast.name: Mae
supporting_cast.secret: Unintentionally feeds Grant information about Lena's state through board communications.

supporting_cast.name: Detective Cross
supporting_cast.secret: Receives the archive duplicate from Calder in Chapter Seventeen; acts on it only after Lena's evidence sequence is complete.

central_mystery.question: Who is actually controlling what Calder observes — and will Lena's strategy survive the settlement without Calder overriding her plan?
central_mystery.answer: Lena detected Calder's surveillance in Chapter Three. From that point she controlled portions of what he could see — repeated routines, red receipts, door seals, a paper planner, and a certified honeytoken. She designed the evidence trap that forced Grant to commit to a false chain of custody at the settlement. Calder believed he was the watcher; he was the watched. The decisive sequence of visible events was directed by Lena, not Calder or Grant.

bloodline.description: Lena and Calder are strangers with no shared bloodline. Grant is Lena's estranged husband. Mae is Lena's biological sister. Detective Cross is a former colleague of Calder, unrelated by blood.
hard_rules: female_lead và male_lead KHÔNG cùng huyết thống
No secret twin, impostor, body double, memory-loss twist, hidden pregnancy, or false identity twist.
No child, pregnancy, or custody subplot.
No named character outside the locked cast.

world_rules: All surveillance is external to Lena's apartment; no hidden cameras inside her home.
Evidence must be physical or independently verifiable; no digital deus ex machina.
No violence, guns, knives, or physical assault.
No police action based on a single recording or accusation; no instant arrest.
No scene outside Calder's first-person POV.
No new evidence introduced after Chapter Fifteen.

series_arc.thesis: Calder is hired to observe Lena and report instability, but Lena detects him and begins controlling what he sees. Grant escalates gaslighting toward a forced property settlement. Calder must decide between possession and preservation of evidence.
series_arc.ending_hook: Lena asks Calder to return without recording equipment. She chooses when he enters, when he watches, and when the curtain closes. The thriller question is resolved: Lena controlled the decisive sequence. The romance question remains: once no longer useful, does she want him?

content_rules: Explicit sexual content only in Chapters Eleven and Eighteen, with affirmative consent and camera off.
No sexual contact before Chapter Ten.
No portrayal of Lena's Chapter Eight action as certainty that Calder recorded the envelope theft.
No romance payoff for Calder ignoring Lena's refusal.
Chapter Sixteen: Lena withdraws access; Calder obeys immediately.
Chapter Seventeen: Calder enters without romantic reconciliation.
No hallucination explanation for Lena's observations.
No Book Two villain appearing in Book One.
